name: duo-start
works_with: Claude Code as a plugin. Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI and others through the skills CLI
short: The starting point for getting an iOS app ready for iPhone Duo: it checks your app, runs a first pass and picks the next Duology skill.
what: duo-start is the entry skill of Duology, a pack of 30 skills for Apple's foldable iPhone Duo. It works out whether the app is SwiftUI or UIKit, new or existing, and which SDK it builds with. Then it builds with Xcode 27.1, runs `duo-lint`, checks the app open and closed on the iPhone Duo simulator, writes a short report and routes each problem to one skill.
who: iOS developers with a native SwiftUI or UIKit app who want it to work on iPhone Duo. Flutter, React Native and Capacitor apps aren't covered. The skill points those to another repo.
needs: Xcode 27.1 (27A9275 or later) and the iPhone Duo simulator on iOS 27.1
A coding agent that loads AI skills

steps.title: Or install for other agents
steps.text: The CLI finds your agent and installs every skill. Add `--skill <name>` to install one.

steps.title: Check your setup
steps.text: Restart Claude Code first. It checks macOS, Xcode 27.1, the simulator runtime, the iPhone Duo simulator and Python, and changes nothing on its own. On other agents, ask for it in plain words.

steps.title: Ask your agent
steps.text: Ask it to get your app ready for iPhone Duo. duo-start reports what it found before it fixes anything.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Make my app work well on iPhone Duo. Start with an audit, fix what it finds, then run it on the Duo simulator.

watch: It builds through `DEVELOPER_DIR` pointing at Xcode 27.1 and never runs `sudo` or `xcode-select -s`, so your Mac's default Xcode stays the same.
The simulator has no pose command. You click the pose buttons in Device Hub yourself, unless you give the app that runs your agent Accessibility permission.
Exporting Apple's App Resizability skill changes your setup, so the skill asks before it does it.
Everything so far is checked on the simulator only. Checks on a real iPhone Duo and published test results are planned before v1.0.
The first simulator launch with Xcode 27.1 can take several minutes.
